items.abstract: <jats:p xml:lang="en">This paper outlines the formalization of derived categories in the mathematical library of the proof assistant Lean 4. The derived category D(C) of any abelian category C is formalized as the localization of the category of unbounded cochain complexes with respect to the class of quasi-isomorphisms, and it is endowed with a triangulated structure.</jats:p>
title: Formalization of derived categories in Lean/mathlib
The lean mathematical library

items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper presents a formal verification of the Euler Sieve algorithm — a linear variant of the classical Sieve of Eratosthenes — using the Lean proof assistant. We begin by discussing the traditional Sieve of Eratosthenes and its inherent redundancy when crossing out composite numbers. We then introduce the Euler Sieve, which overcomes this drawback by ensuring that each composite number is “marked” only once, achieving linear time complexity. Finally, we present a Lean formalization that rigorously verifies the correctness of the Euler Sieve, including definitions, lemmas, and the overall rigorous recursive structure. To the best of our knowledge, this work is the first formal proof of the Euler Sieve by an interactive proof assistant.</jats:p>
title: Formal verification of the Euler Sieve via Lean

items.publisher: Springer Science and Business Media LLC
items.abstract: Computational biology software routinely implements kinetic models, survival functions, and structural metrics whose mathematical properties — non- negativity, monotonicity, conservation laws — are assumed but never formally certified. We call this gap the Bio-Algorithm Verification Problem (BAVP): an algorithm computes a biological quantity with known mathematical properties, yet no machine-checkable proof establishes those properties for all valid inputs. Unit tests cannot close BAVP; they verify specific values, not universal statements. We introduce K-Lean, the first sorry-free Lean 4 library for computational biology. K-Lean provides 94 formal contracts spanning protein structure, enzyme kinetics, longevity, clinical medicine, genomics, and epidemiology. Every theorem compiles without sorry under Lean 4 (leanprover/lean4:stable) with Mathlib4. CI gates — lake build followed by grep -r sorry — enforce the zero-sorry invariant on every commit. K-Lean applies to biology what PhysLean demonstrated for physics: type-theoretic proof as a first-class deliverable alongside numerical code. The result is a machine-verifiable certificate layer that regulators (FDA 21 CFR Part 11, EU AI Act Art. 13) and reproducibility auditors can inspect independently of any specific implementation.
title:
K-Lean: Machine-Verified Formal Proofs
for Computational Biology
